title: Clothing holds together: collars, coats and sleeves
items: Collars, apron straps and crossbelts now sit cleanly on the clothes beneath them, with smooth edges and nothing showing through, from the maid and cook to the 1812 soldiers and the children.
Men in coats no longer show a gap under the arm as they walk, and the back vents of the tailcoats and soldiers' coats hang closed.
Sleeve cuffs turn with the wrist as one clean edge, and the coachman's gloves reach up inside his sleeves.
